rationale: Matthew 7:3-5 pictures a specific case of hypocritical judgment: a person who tries to remove "the speck" from a brother's eye while a "beam" sits in his own (BSB). Paul states the same underlying logic as a general argument rather than a specific image. Romans 2:1 opens, "You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things" (Romans 2:1, BSB). Both texts turn a person's own act of judging back onto the judger -- Matthew by picturing an unnoticed, larger fault in the judger's own eye; Paul by stating directly that the one who judges "do[es] the same things" as the one judged. Paul's passage carries no citation formula naming Jesus's saying and does not quote Matthew 7:1-5's own wording, which is why this is graded parallel rather than quotation or doctrinal_synthesis. The label is strong because the shared logical structure (judging another exposes the judger's own comparable fault) and the shared word "judge" are both directly checkable in each text's own wording, not an inference this connection is adding.
